# CPL rotations (JLC) — generated by `design/pcb/scripts/l6_fab.py`, do not edit

JLC rotation = KiCad rotation + correction (mod 360). KiCad's 0° is the IPC-7351B zero orientation of the footprint file (pin 1 top-left on ICs, pad 1 on the left on two-terminal parts). JLC's 0° is the 0° of the part's model in JLC's library. **The corrections are the widely used KiCad → JLC values (SOT-23 family +180°, QFN / SON family +270°, CP_Elec +180°, everything else 0°), recalled, not fetched: UNVERIFIED.** JLC's online preview could not be used (no upload by the team, H2), so the owner checks every orientation-sensitive part below in JLC's 3-D / assembly preview at order time and fixes the rotation there if a part shows turned.

How to check one part: in JLC's preview (top view, north = the RJ45 / buttons edge at the top) the part's pin-1 dot / cathode band / + mark must sit on the side given in the last column. That column comes from the board itself (where pad 1 is), so it is right whatever JLC's 0° convention is. The assembly drawing `assembly-top-refs.pdf` shows the same pad with a filled dot.

Mid X / Mid Y = centre of the bounding box of all the part's pads (origin: panel lower-left, y up, the same origin as the Gerbers and the drill files). For parts whose KiCad origin is not that centre, the shift is listed at the end.
